To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the induction and impairment of vection is dependent on inertial motion amplitude and that saturated vection was more robust for translations.

saturated vection can be induced by applying inertial motion to a human subject and that saturated vection cannot be maintained when the subject is exposed to inertial motion above a certain amplitude.
the induction and impairment of saturated vections are similar for yaw and surge, but that the inertial motion am plitudes needed to induce and impair the two types of vection are not identical.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model of the perception of self motion.
the perception of self-acceleration, visual scene acceleration and visual scene decelerations.
the perception of motion, specifically, with the perception of self- and world motion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the perception of self-velocity and the visual scene velocity are independent of the perception of inertial motions.
the subjects perceived a sudden change from a zero velocity to a constant velocity and that the constant velocity was the saturated velocity.

the induction of saturated yaw and/or surge vection is not a function of the inertial motions, but the perception of additional self-motion during saturated vection is a function of the amplitudes of the applied inertial movements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the induction and impairment of saturated vections are not due to the same mechanisms.
the subjects perceived the applied inertial accelerations as a change in self-motion and visual motion, but not as self-acceleration and visual deceleration.
the perception of self-acceleration and visual scene decelerations is a function of the magnitude of the inertial motion and the duration of the inertial motions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inertial motions that can impair saturated vection depend on the vection direction.
the perception of vection is not a passive phenomenon, but rather a dynamic process that is affected by the motion of the observer, the visual environment, and the observer’s attention.
the perception of self-acceleration and visual scene decelerations during the induction of vection is not a prerequisite for the perception of vection.
